paper.title: G-Memory: Tracing Hierarchical Memory for Multi-Agent Systems
paper.central_claim: G-Memory, a three-tier (insight/query/interaction) agentic memory that evolves from collaborative trajectories, is a plug-and-play module that improves MAS success/accuracy (up to 20.89% embodied, 10.12% QA) without modifying the host frameworks.

signatures.object: per-agent memory state Mem_i injected into each agent of a host MAS (AutoGen/DyLAN/MacNet); backing store = three-tier graph (insight / query / interaction)
signatures.information: new query text, stored query nodes (query, Failed/Resolved status, interaction graph), role description of each agent; no weights; LLM relevance rater and LLM graph sparsifier see stored trajectories
signatures.operation: embedding top-k over query graph -> 1-hop expansion -> upward projection to insights, downward LLM-sparsified core trajectories -> role-conditioned projection Phi into each agent memory
signatures.output: role-specific insight + trajectory snippets prepended to agent context at query start
signatures.conditions: host MAS unchanged; invoked once at query onset; k in {1,2}, M in {2..5}
signatures.feedback: environment execution status (Failed/Resolved) after each query
signatures.selection_rule: cosine similarity + LLM relevancy score 1-10 for top-M; no outcome-based admission
signatures.persistence: all three graph levels persist across queries
signatures.later_use: every subsequent query in the same benchmark stream
signatures.claimed_effect: up to +20.89 (ALFWorld) and +10.12 (knowledge QA) over no-memory; avg gains across 5 benchmarks x 3 MAS x 3 backbones
signatures.failure_boundary: more hops / larger k add noise; ChatDev-M/MacNet-M/Voyager/MemoryBank sometimes degrade

signatures.object: the persisted graph store itself (insight nodes + supporting-query sets + query edges)
signatures.information: completed trajectory, task status, previously used insights
signatures.operation: LLM summarization of success/failure contrast into new insight; add query node with edges to top-M relevant and insight-supporting queries; extend supporting sets of used insights
signatures.conditions: none beyond task completion; failed tasks also written
signatures.selection_rule: none described (every query writes); consolidation prompt in appendix with an unspecified invocation rule
signatures.claimed_effect: evolving memory yields progressive improvement (trial curves)
signatures.failure_boundary: not reported: no staleness, conflict, rollback or harmful-insight analysis

gap.author_gap: MAS memory is overly simplistic (inside-trial or final-artifact only) and lacks cross-trial and agent-specific customization; single-agent memories do not carry over to MAS because trajectories are far longer.
gap.checked_gap: Partly corroborated inside the paper: adapted single-agent memories and MAS-native memories frequently fail to help or lower accuracy (E007). The token-length premise rests on a figure not readable in text. The gap is a real, non-weight object (agent memory), but the claimed bottleneck (flat memory vs hierarchical memory) is not tested against a matched flat insight+trajectory store.
lineage: inside-trial chat memory: MemoryBank, MemGPT (per paper text)
cross-trial single-agent: ExpeL, Synapse, Generative Agents, Voyager
MAS-native memory: MetaGPT, ChatDev, MacNet (final-artifact passing)
automated MAS design: GPTSwarm, ADAS, AFlow, MaAS (one-shot, no accumulation)

rs_pattern.reason: Frozen LLMs in a host MAS are conditioned on retrieved insights and sparsified past trajectories with no parameter updates (adapt_via_conditioning). C03 not assigned under the run convention (r03a A-MEM, r03b Dynamic Cheatsheet): no category-level holdout and no equal-budget flat-retrieval control (C03 steps 4–5); the hierarchical store organisation that is the contribution is carried by domain H04. heterogeneous_decomposition (sol) not kept: the insight/interaction split is a multi-granularity index design, not a partition of a resource by an empirically characterised property.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: C03 not claimed: C03 centers on an upstream phase teaching a model to parse a schema and on category-level holdout; G-Memory is pure inference-time retrieval conditioning with no upstream phase. Overlap only with the retrieval-as-first-class-input sub-move.
matches.success_checks: ablation toggling the conditioning (no-memory vs memory) present; category/structural holdout absent; contamination audit absent
matches.failure_checks: multi-component pipeline with shallow ablation (only insights vs interactions): present; evaluation of idealized access: not applicable
matches.reason: Operation is: express a new query as retrieved insights and trajectories injected as context so a frozen MAS solves it without parameter updates. That is the card operation, but the card family is about trained conditioning channels; fit is partial.
Store is reshaped into a three-tier graph with promotion/linking (query->insight support sets) and retrieval by traversal; claim rests on organization and traversal design (H04).
Insight nodes are LLM lessons from contrasting failed and successful trajectories (prompt in Appendix C), but the lesson layer is one tier of a larger index.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Both retrieve stored precedent and inject as context without weight updates; domain card adds store structure (tiers, graph, traversal) and write path that the RS card does not specify.
pattern_mapping.conditions_differences: RS card expects structural holdout and contamination audit; domain card adds selective retrieval, write gating, store-removal certification. Paper meets selective retrieval, partly store-removal, not write gating or holdout.

assessment.evidence_level_note: Later queries read graph entries written after earlier queries (case study: a different ALFWorld query retrieved), and the No-memory host MAS is a store-off control in all nine MAS×backbone settings. Construction stream = evaluation stream (prequential), label-derived status on QA, ALFWorld trial protocol undefined; no frozen-store or held-out evaluation → not transfer/improver. Same level as in-stream memory precedents (r03a A-MEM, r03b Dynamic Cheatsheet).
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported, single runs: on five benchmarks × three host MAS × three backbones the plug-in raises scores over No-memory (avg +5.5 to +10.7) and over author-adapted memory baselines by smaller margins (e.g. Qwen-7b avg +3.61 AutoGen, +2.40 MacNet vs the best baseline, not the 6.8/5.5 stated in §5.2). Both tiers contribute on two benchmarks; insights matter slightly more than the prose says. Not reproduced.
unresolved: No held-out stream or order control; hop/k/M chosen on reported benchmarks (opus:O07).
No sample sizes, repeats or intervals.
Two prose/table mismatches (opus:O01, opus:O06); Table values used.

G.reason: Opus sides with sol. The non-weight object (MAS memory) and its stated bottleneck are concrete and the lineage is laid out, but the closest neighbour is ExpeL, whose insight prompts G-Memory adapts (Appendix C credit), and ExpeL / A-Mem / Mem0 are distinguished only in prose (son55:E016); the 'flat vs hierarchical' residue is never tested and the 10× token premise rests on an unreadable figure. Adapted-baseline degradations (son55:E007) are author re-implementations, not an independent diagnosis. Consistent with A-MEM (r03a) and Dynamic Cheatsheet (r03b) G=2.

M.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Retrieve → hop-expand → upward insights / downward LLM-sparsified trajectories → role projection → three-level write is reconstructable from equations and prompts and makes checkable predictions (role-specific delivery matters; over-retrieval hurts) that are partly tested.

X.reason: Opus sides with son55. Retrieval and write steps are explicit, but retention governance is thin: every query (failed or resolved) is written, the merge prompt has no stated trigger, there is no versioning, retirement or rollback, and invocation order/initial state are unspecified. sol's 3 credits sensitivity analysis (an E item) to execution. Same as A-MEM (r03a) / Dynamic Cheatsheet (r03b) X=2.

E.measurement.reason: Opus sides with son55 and adds two reporting errors. Benchmark metrics (success, progress rate, EM) are standard, but the prose claims a 6.8 / 5.5 average margin over the best baselines where Table 3 gives +3.61 / +2.40 (opus:O01–O05), the ablation prose inverts which tier matters more (opus:O06), the AutoGen host contains a reference-standard agent and the ALFWorld multi-trial protocol is undefined. sol's 3 did not register the mismatches.

E.causality.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. No-memory control in every setting, six author-adapted alternative memories and a two-tier ablation on two benchmarks; no equal-budget flat store, no role-projection / sparsifier / query-graph ablation, and best-baseline margins are 1–4 points per cell in single runs.

E.holdout.reason: Both seats 1; re-checked. Memory is built from the scored queries with label-derived status on QA (opus:O08), hop/k/M are fixed on the reported benchmarks (opus:O07), the AutoGen host has a reference-standard agent, no order control or contamination check; breadth over 5 benchmarks × 3 backbones only partly offsets.

E.statistics.reason: Opus sides with sol under the frozen A2 ladder: rung 1 needs reported sample sizes plus negative results; G-Memory reports neither N per benchmark nor repeats, seeds, intervals or tests (son55 itself infers N from percentages). Baseline negative deltas and direction consistency across nine settings are not a substitute for the missing statistics.
